messages:
mara: quick heads-up — I ran an internal burstbench against prod-sim to try and pick sane defaults for RPM/TPM + burst window. started seeing sustained 429s and a spike in retries that would have caused a billing bump if this were real traffic. logs and repro below. anyone who owns rate-limits or quota math: pls weigh in.

sanjay: what profile did you run? single long-lived conn or lots of short ones? :thinking:

mara: many short clients. config: 200 parallel clients, 3 rps each, 60s ramp + 60s steady. payload ~600 tokens (chat.generate). quick curl we used:

```bash
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat.generate\" 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"open-inf-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<~600 token payload>"}],"max_tokens":512}'
```

mara: sample response spamming the logs:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 360
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670000123
{
  "error": {"message":"rate limit exceeded","type":"quota_exhausted"}
}
```

lex: hmm X-RateLimit-Limit 360 — is that per-api-key or per-org? If per-key and we had 200 clients reusing the key, we'd blow through quickly.

ellie: also saw a handful of 401s in earlier run when we were rotating the test key from CI. stack trace shows token validation failing at the proxy cache layer. 401s confuse clients and lead to immediate retries (and billing). sample: `{"error":"invalid_token","message":"token revoked"}`

kevin: ops-bot noted p95 latency ~420ms p99 ~1.2s during steady state. error rate ~4.7% during the two minutes after ramp. ops-bot: run summary: `clients=200, rps_total=600, requests=72000, 429s=3380 (4.7%)` :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ops-bot: automated: test-run: 2029-07-24T18:10:00Z; infra=prod-sim; commit=ef3a1b9; dashboard=https://dash.internal/runs/1891234567

mara: reproduction steps (short):
1) export TEST_KEY (org-scoped)
2) run vegeta attack: `echo \"POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat.generate\" | vegeta attack -duration=2m -rate=600 -connections=200 -body=payload.json | vegeta report`
3) observe 429s in response body / X-RateLimit-* headers

sanjay: thanks. I think two interacting things: our default free-tier RPM and the burst token bucket window are too small for multi-connection clients. proposal: drop default documented RPM to 300 and set burst tokens to 1200 with a 60s refill window (i.e., allow 4x burst). Also ensure docs emphasize connection reuse and client-side jitter/backoff.

ellie: +1 on docs. we should also add a short circuit for 401s and classify them as auth failures (no retry) in SDKs. that avoids billing spikes from immediate retries.

kevin: for Dedicated/Dedicated-sim we should allow higher RPMs or a per-customer override. For hosted free tier, 300 rpm + 1200 burst seems conservative and would have prevented most 429s in my quick sim.

mara: added a sample rate-limit config I put in the run repo:
```json
{"rate_limit_type":"leaky_bucket","rpm":"300","burst_tokens":"1200","window_secs":"60","enforce_scope":"per_api_key"}
```

lex: note: we use token-bucket semantics internally, not leaky bucket — minor naming but important for math. with token-bucket and refill=burst_tokens/window a 1200/60s gives 20 tokens/s baseline which equals 1200 rpm? wait, do the conversions carefully. recommend we add a helper doc showing conversions for RPM/TPM/burst.

mara: agreed. for clarity: 300 rpm = 5 rps baseline. burst 1200 tokens over 60s => short bursts up to ~400 rps for a few seconds depending on client pattern. that's the behaviour we want for transient spikes but prevents long sustained storms.

support-bot: note: customer-facing impact: if clients retry immediately on 429 with no jitter, will multiply the traffic and can push through billing unexpectedly. suggests adding a warning in the billing docs and an example retry policy (exponential backoff, random jitter).

kevin: action items I can pick up: (1) run a parameter sweep for rpm in [200,300,360,480] and burst in [600,1200,2400] on prod-sim and upload results to the dashboard; (2) open a docs PR for retry guidance + example SDK change to avoid retrying on 401.

mara: i'll attach the vegeta output + raw logs to the ticket. also putting a short note for support: if a customer reports latency + billing spike, ask if they recently rotated keys or had a CI job that created a burst of parallel short-lived connections. that matches what we saw.

ellie: one more thing — quota exhaustion currently returns 429 without a structured `retry_after` in body for all endpoints. we should standardize the `Retry-After` header and add guidance for SDKs to honor it. small PR in rate-limiter to add Retry-After when possible.

sanjay: i'll draft the math doc and ping infra to confirm our token accounting.

mara: cool. I'll file internal ticket: SRE-7021 with summary + logs + reproducer. assigning to kevin for the sweep. tagging @sanjay and @ellie for doc/SDK follow-ups. thanks :thumbsup:

kevin: got it — will start sweep tomorrow and paste results here.

mara: thanks team. closing the loop here, will update ticket when we have the sweep matrix and recommended defaults.
